lines: Oscillator with five waveforms available at once, among them an even wave carrying the fundamental and its even harmonics
Sets the octave in ten steps, marked as organ footage from 32 foot down to 1/16 foot
Tunes the oscillator over -7 to +7 semitones
Sets the width of the square wave, held between 5% and 95% unless the menu allows the full sweep
Volt-per-octave pitch, added to the other V/OCT input and to the octave and tune knobs
Exponential frequency modulation, scaled so that 4V shifts the pitch by one octave
A rising edge here restarts every waveform half way through its cycle
Modulates the width of the square wave; the voltage is divided by 5 and added to the PWM knob
A triangle wave, 10V peak to peak
A sine wave, 10V peak to peak
A saw at twice the fundamental mixed with a sine at the fundamental, which leaves the fundamental and its even harmonics
A sawtooth wave, 10V peak to peak
A square wave, 10V peak to peak, its width set by the PWM knob
Menu — Hardware compatibility puts back the DC offset that an off-centre pulse has on the hardware, and lifts the 5% to 95% limit on pulse width
Menu — Oversampling runs the waveform generation at up to eight times the sample rate to cut aliasing, with x4 the default
Two ramp generators that also work as slew limiters, envelope followers and function generators, with a logic section combining the two
Picks the time range for that channel: Fast spans 1ms to 1 second, Medium spans 10ms to 10 seconds, and Slow spans 100ms to 100 seconds
Bends the slope of that channel, logarithmic counter-clockwise, straight at noon and exponential clockwise
Fires that channel's ramp by hand, one ramp per press
Sets how long that channel takes to rise, from the shortest time its RANGE switch allows through to 1024 times that
Sets how long that channel takes to fall, from the shortest time its RANGE switch allows through to 1024 times that
Makes that channel retrigger itself the moment it finishes falling, so it runs as an oscillator
Attenuates one ramp against the other before the comparator, MIN and MAX outputs: counter-clockwise lowers B, clockwise lowers A, and at noon both pass at full level
The signal that channel slews, its rise and fall times limiting how fast the output can follow it
A rising edge sends that channel's ramp to 10V and then back down; it reads high above 4V and low below 0.2V
Lengthens that channel's rise time, each volt doubling it, and is added to the RISE knob
Lengthens that channel's fall time, each volt doubling it, and is added to the FALL knob
Shortens both the rise and the fall time of that channel, each volt halving them
Switches cycling on for that channel while it stands at 4V or more, and is added to the CYCLE switch
That channel's ramp, 0-10V, or its input signal slewed by the rise and fall times
A 10V gate for as long as that channel's output is climbing
A 10V gate for as long as that channel's output is dropping
A 1ms 10V pulse the moment that channel finishes falling
10V while ramp B stands above ramp A and 0V otherwise, both taken after BALANCE
Whichever of the two ramps is lower at each moment, taken after BALANCE
Whichever of the two ramps is higher at each moment, taken after BALANCE
Two four-quadrant multipliers, each working out A times B plus C, with a voltage-controlled offset
Attenuates and inverts the B input of that section before it multiplies A, from x-2 through zero to x2
Attenuates and inverts the C input of that section before it is added, from x-1 through zero to x1
One factor of the multiplication in that section; it is multiplied by B and divided by 5V
The other factor of the multiplication in that section, scaled by the B level knob; with nothing patched it stands at 5V, which turns the knob into a plain attenuverter for A
The offset added to the product in that section, scaled by the C level knob; with nothing patched it stands at 10V, which turns the knob into an offset control
The first section's result, clipped; with no cable here that result is passed on and added into OUT 2 instead
The second section's result, clipped, with the first section's result added in when OUT 1 has no cable
Spring reverb, a convolution of a real spring tank, with two inputs driving the tank and both a wet and a mixed output
Crossfades the MIX output between the dry signal at IN 1 and the reverb
Sets how hard that input drives the spring tank, marked from -12dBu to 14dBu
Sets the high-pass filter on the signal going into the tank, from 200Hz to 4000Hz
Scales the drive of the input on that side, 0-10V spanning nothing to the full drive its slider sets; with nothing patched the drive is whatever the slider says
An audio input into the spring tank, and the only signal fed to the dry side of the MIX output
An audio input into the spring tank, which never reaches the dry side of the MIX output
Shifts the dry and wet balance at the MIX output; the voltage is divided by 10 and added to the balance knob
The dry signal at IN 1 crossfaded with the reverb, clamped to -10V to 10V
The reverb on its own with no dry signal, clamped to -10V to 10V
SpringReverb.notes: The peak lamp and the seven-segment VU meter have no census indices, so they have no lines.

lines: Four-channel mixer for audio or CV, with a straight output and an inverted one
Sets the level of that channel in the mix, from silence to unity gain
A signal into the mix, scaled by that channel's level knob
The four channels added together, with no clipping
The four channels added together and inverted, with no clipping
Lag processor limiting how fast its output can follow its input, with separate rise and fall times
Bends the slope, straight counter-clockwise and increasingly curved clockwise as the gap to the input shrinks
Sets how long the output takes to climb, from 1ms up to 100 seconds for a 10V step
Sets how long the output takes to drop, from 1ms up to 100 seconds for a 10V step
Lengthens the rise time, each volt cutting the slope further, and is added to the rise slider
Lengthens the fall time, each volt cutting the slope further, and is added to the fall slider
The signal to be slewed
The input signal with its rate of change limited by the rise and fall times
Note — with the module bypassed the input is passed straight to the output
SlewLimiter.notes: The IN jack and the OUT jack carry whatever is patched in, audio or CV, so neither has a family.

lines: Two attenuverters, each scaling and inverting a signal and adding a fixed offset to it
Scales that channel's input from x-1 through zero to x1, inverting it anti-clockwise of noon
Adds a fixed voltage to that channel after its attenuverter, -10V to 10V
The signal to be scaled and offset
That channel's input scaled by its attenuverter with its offset added, clamped to -10V to 10V
Four percussive envelope generators, each with a VCA and a channel of a mixer, and a choke on each pair
Sets the level of that channel in the mix, squared so the bottom of the travel is fine-grained
Sets how long that channel's envelope takes to fall, from 4.5ms to 4 seconds; the attack is fixed at 1.5ms
Silences the second channel of that pair for as long as the first channel's envelope is in its attack
The signal that channel's VCA passes; with nothing patched, the even channel of a pair takes the signal from the odd one
Scales the gain of all four channels and their envelope outputs, 0-10V under a square root, so 10V gives full level; with nothing patched all four run at full level
A rising edge fires that channel's envelope; it reads high above 2V and low below 0.1V
Lengthens that channel's decay, 10V covering half the travel of its decay slider, and is added to it
That channel's signal after its VCA, which takes it out of the mix; the fourth channel's jack carries the mix instead and always includes its own channel
That channel's envelope as a voltage, 0-10V at full strength
Six VCAs with adjustable response curves, cascading into one mix
Bends that channel's response curve, exponential counter-clockwise, straight at noon and logarithmic clockwise
Sets that channel's output level after its VCA, from silence to unity gain
The signal that channel's VCA passes
Sets that channel's gain, 0-10V from silence to full; with nothing patched the channel runs at full gain
That channel's signal after its VCA and level knob, which takes it out of the mix; the sixth channel's jack carries the mix instead and always includes its own channel
Menu — Final row is mix turns the cascading mix off, so every channel's jack carries only its own signal
Note — with the module bypassed each input is passed straight to the output on its own row
Two wavefolders with different curves, plus a chopper that switches between them under a gate or at the input's zero crossings
Drives channel A into its wavefolder, from silence through unity to a hard fold
Drives channel B into its wavefolder, from silence through unity to a hard fold
Attenuates and inverts the CV feeding that channel's fold amount, from x-1 through zero to x1
The signal folded by channel A, and the signal whose zero crossings drive the chopper when the CHOPP input has no cable
The signal folded by channel B; with nothing patched here the A input feeds both channels
A gate switching the CHOPP output between the two channels, high for A and low for B; with nothing patched, channel A's zero crossings do the switching instead
Adds to that channel's fold amount, 10V covering the whole range, after that channel's attenuverter; channel B falls back to channel A's attenuated CV when nothing is patched
Adds to that channel's fold amount, 10V covering the whole range, with no attenuverter in the way
The two folded channels cut together, following the CHOPP gate or channel A's zero crossings, with its DC removed by default
Channel A after its wavefolder
Channel B after its wavefolder
Menu — Block DC on Chopp takes the DC offset out of the chopped output
Menu — Oversampling runs the wavefolders at up to sixteen times the sample rate to cut aliasing, with x4 the default
ChoppingKinky.notes: The oversampling default was read from the source; the menu offers Off, x2, x4, x8 and x16.

lines: Bass drum voice: a sine core through a wave shaper, with a pitch envelope and a decay envelope
Sets the base pitch of the drum, from 27.5Hz to 123.47Hz
Fires the drum by hand, one hit per press
Bends the sine core towards a square as it is turned up
Sets how long the drum takes to fade, from 0.075 seconds to 4 seconds
Sets how long the pitch envelope takes to fall, from 0.0075 seconds to 1 second
Sets how far the pitch envelope lifts the pitch at the start of the hit, reaching 10000Hz at the top of its travel
A rising edge fires the drum; it reads high above 4V and low below 0.2V
Sets the output level, 0-10V from silence to full; with nothing patched the level is full
Volt-per-octave pitch: each volt doubles the base pitch that TUNE sets
Adds to the SHAPE knob, 0-10V covering its whole range
Lengthens the fade by a tenth of a second per volt, added to the decay slider, and the result is held between 0.01 seconds and 10 seconds
The finished bass drum, reaching 10V peak to peak at full level
Kickall.notes: The envelope lamp beside the shape knob has no census index, so it has no line.

lines: Sample and hold with a clock of its own that reaches audio rate, and an eight-step switch deciding which ticks fire
Sets the sampling rate of the internal clock, from 1Hz up to well past audio rate
Tunes the internal clock over one octave above whatever RATE sets
Picks whether the internal clock times the sampling, or the CLOCK/SYNC input does
Picks what that step does: On fires a sample, Off skips it, and Reset ends the pattern there so the sequence restarts from step 1
In external mode a rising edge here takes a sample; in internal mode it resets the internal clock's phase, hard-syncing it. It reads high above 2V and low below 0.1V
Volt-per-octave control of the internal clock rate, added to the RATE and FINE knobs
A rising edge here takes a sample outside the clock's own timing, reading high above 2V and low below 0.1V
The signal being sampled
A 10V square wave at the internal clock rate, at 50% duty
A trigger on each step switched On, at 50% duty when internally clocked and a short pulse when externally clocked
The input sampled and held at each firing step, holding its value until the next one
Menu — Remove DC Offset centres the clock and trigger outputs around 0V instead of running them from 0V upwards
SamplingModulator.notes: The RAW input and the SAMPLED output carry audio or CV depending on what is patched, so neither has a family.

lines: Four crossfaders driven by one fader, each blending an A input into a B input, with a cascading mix
Attenuates the CV 1 input before it is added to the fader position
Attenuates that channel's A input before the crossfade, from silence to unity gain
Attenuates that channel's B input before the crossfade, from silence to unity gain
Picks the crossfade law for that channel: Audio keeps the power constant through the middle, CV keeps the sum constant
Sets how long the fader takes to reach a new position, from 0.01 seconds to 15 seconds
Crossfades every channel between its A input and its B input
Moves every channel towards B, 0-10V covering the whole sweep, after the attenuator and added to the fader position
Sets that channel's crossfade outright, 0-10V running from A to B and overriding both the fader and CV 1; with nothing patched the channel follows CV 1 and the fader
The A side of that channel's crossfade, scaled by its A level knob; with nothing patched it stands at 10V, which makes the knob a constant source
The B side of that channel's crossfade, scaled by its B level knob; with nothing patched it stands at 10V, which makes the knob a constant source
That channel's crossfade, which takes it out of the mix; the fourth channel's jack carries the mix instead and always includes its own channel
Morphader.notes: The A and B input jacks and the four output jacks carry audio or CV depending on what is patched and on the per-channel mode switch, so they have no family.

lines: ADSR envelope generator with a variable curve and a gate output for each of its four stages
Picks how the envelope responds to its gate: Gate holds the sustain for as long as the gate is high, Trigger runs attack and decay right through on a single edge
Raises the gate by hand, held high for as long as the button is pressed
Bends the curve of every stage, straight counter-clockwise and increasingly curved clockwise
Sets how long the envelope takes to climb to full, from 3ms to 10 seconds
Sets how long the envelope takes to fall from full to the sustain level, from 3ms to 10 seconds
Sets the level the envelope holds at while the gate stays high, 0-10V at the output
Sets how long the envelope takes to fall to zero once the gate drops, from 3ms to 10 seconds
A rising edge starts the envelope and a high level holds its sustain
Shortens or lengthens the attack, 10V covering the whole travel of the attack slider, and is added to it
Shortens or lengthens the decay, 10V covering the whole travel of the decay slider, and is added to it
Shifts the sustain level, 10V covering the whole travel of the sustain slider, and is added to it
Shortens or lengthens the release, 10V covering the whole travel of the release slider, and is added to it
The envelope itself, 0-10V
A 10V gate for as long as the envelope is in its attack stage
A 10V gate for as long as the envelope is in its decay stage
A 10V gate for as long as the envelope is holding at the sustain level
A 10V gate for as long as the envelope is in its release stage
Four-channel stereo mixer in 6HP, with an extra stereo pair that bypasses the level knobs
Sets the level of that channel in the mix, from silence up through unity to a boost
The left side of that channel, and with nothing patched on the right it feeds both sides in mono
The right side of that channel; with nothing patched here the left input feeds both sides
The left side of the auxiliary pair, which goes straight into the mix at unity gain with no level knob
The right side of the auxiliary pair, which goes straight into the mix at unity gain; with nothing patched here the auxiliary left input feeds both sides
The left side of the mix
The right side of the mix
Eight-step sequential switch, gate generator and step sequencer: one signal routed to or from eight jacks under a clock, with a gain and a gate on every step
Picks which step the switch is on, one step per position; turned fully anti-clockwise to RUN, the step advances with the clock instead
Sets what the gate outputs do on each step: no gate, one gate filling the step, one gate at 50% duty, or between 2 and 8 gates spread through the step
Starts and stops the sequence: pushed up it plays and a second push stops it, pushed down it resets and plays one cycle through
Multiplies or divides the clock driving the sequence, from a sixteenth of the incoming rate up to sixteen times it
Attenuates the signal passing through the switch on that step, from silence to unity gain
Sets how many gates each step carries, a volt per gate up to 10V, with the GATE MODE knob attenuating it
Selects the step, a volt per step, added to the ADDRESS knob
The clock driving the sequence, read high above 2V and low below 0.1V; with nothing patched an internal clock runs instead, set by tap tempo on the menu
A rising edge sends the playhead back to the start; from stopped it also plays one cycle through
A signal normalled into every step jack that has no cable of its own; with nothing patched here it stands at 10V, which the menu can change to 1V or 5V
In 1 input to 8 outputs mode, the signal routed out to whichever step is current
In 8 inputs to 1 output mode, this step's signal, passed to the COM output while the step is current and scaled by that step's gain slider
A 10V clock, multiplied or divided from the incoming clock by its own setting on the menu
A 10V gate on that step, following the pattern the GATE MODE knob sets, and silent while the sequence is stopped
In 1 input to 8 outputs mode, the COM signal scaled by the current step's gain slider, carried here whenever that step's own output has no cable
In 8 inputs to 1 output mode, the current step's input scaled by that step's gain slider
A 10V gate whenever the current step's gate is high, so it carries the gate pattern of every step in turn
A 1ms 10V pulse when the eighth step ends
In 1 input to 8 outputs mode, the COM signal scaled by that step's gain slider while the step is current, and 0V the rest of the time
Menu — Input/Output mode swaps the module between 1 input and 8 outputs and 8 inputs and 1 output; the jacks change colour to show which way round they are, and cables on them are cleared
Menu — Input clock and Output clock set separate multiplications and divisions, and Tap to set internal tempo sets the internal clock when nothing is patched into the clock input
Menu — Quadratic only mode limits both the clock settings and the gate counts to powers of two
Menu — Output clock follows play/stop silences the clock output whenever the sequence is stopped
Muxlicer.notes: The COM, ALL and step jacks carry whatever is patched through the switch, audio or CV, so they have no family. The ALL and COM positions each hold both an input and an output index, only one of which is live at a time, and both are tagged.

lines: Gate expander for Muxlicer, giving one more gate output whose behaviour is set step by step; it goes immediately to the right of a Muxlicer, or to the right of another Mex chained to one
Picks what the output does on that step: the gate input passed through, silence, or the gate pattern Muxlicer's GATE MODE knob sets
A gate passed through on any step switched to it, squared up if it is not already a gate; with nothing patched here Muxlicer's own clock output is used instead
A 10V gate built step by step from the switch settings, silent while the Muxlicer is stopped
Two digital noise generators running one algorithm each from a library of banks, with a resonant filter on each, plus a third section of grit and white noise
Moves the first of the two parameters the current algorithm exposes; what it changes depends on which algorithm is loaded
Moves the second of the two parameters the current algorithm exposes; what it changes depends on which algorithm is loaded
Sets the cutoff of that section's filter, from 5.8Hz to 11800Hz
Sets the resonance of that section's filter, raising its Q from 0.7 up to about 11
Attenuates the cutoff CV for that section, squared so the bottom of the travel is fine-grained
Picks that section's filter type: lowpass, bandpass or highpass
Turning it steps through the algorithms of the current bank; a click swaps which of the two sections it edits, and a hold of half a second switches it to stepping through banks instead
Sets the density of the gritty noise, from 0.1 events per second up to 20000
Sets the resonance of the filter on the noise section, raising its Q from 0.5 up to about 20
Sets the cutoff of the filter on the noise section, from 8.2Hz to 22050Hz
Picks which noise the filter takes: the gritty noise or the white noise
Moves the first algorithm parameter for that section, -10V to 10V covering the whole range, and is added to the X knob
Moves the second algorithm parameter for that section, -10V to 10V covering the whole range, and is added to the Y knob
Shifts that section's filter cutoff, scaled by that section's cutoff CV attenuator
Steps through the programs of the current bank for that section, half a volt per program, counted on from the program already chosen
Shifts the density of the gritty noise, -10V to 10V covering the whole range, and is added to the grit knob
Shifts the cutoff of the filter on the noise section, scaled by that section's cutoff CV attenuator
That section's noise algorithm through its filter, soft-clipped and reaching 10V peak to peak
Sparse random impulses whose density the grit knob sets, reaching 10V peak to peak
Either the gritty noise or the white noise through a resonant filter, with an asymmetric saturation adding even harmonics
White noise, reaching 10V peak to peak
Menu — Program A and Program B pick the algorithm for each section by name, from four banks: Textures, HH Clusters, Harsh & Wild, and Test
Menu — Remove DC takes the DC offset out of all three outputs, and Bypass Filters passes the raw noise with no filtering
NoisePlethora.notes: The cutoff CV attenuator for the noise section (param 16) and the one for sections A and B behave the same way and share a line. The two seven-segment displays and the bank lamp have no census indices, so they have no lines.

lines: Stereo channel strip: three-band EQ, pan, mute and a voltage-controlled level, with a limiter on the output
Lifts or cuts a low shelf at 125Hz, -20dB to 20dB
Lifts or cuts a peaking band at 1200Hz, -12.5dB to 12.5dB
Lifts or cuts a high shelf at 2000Hz, -15dB to 15dB
Places the signal between left and right
Adds 6dB of gain before the EQ and the VCA
Takes 6dB off after the VCA
Mutes the channel: a click toggles the mute, dragging up unmutes it, and dragging down unmutes it only while the mouse is held
Attenuates the pan CV input, from nothing through to its full effect
Sets the level, -60dB to 0dB
The left side of the signal, and with nothing patched on the right it feeds both sides in mono
Scales the level, 0-10V from silence to whatever the level knob sets; with nothing patched the level is whatever the knob says
The right side of the signal; with nothing patched here the left input feeds both sides
Moves the signal between left and right, -5V to 5V covering the whole sweep, after the pan CV attenuator and added to the pan knob
The left side of the finished signal
The right side of the finished signal
Menu — Apply Highpass puts a 25Hz high-pass on the signal, Apply Highshelf puts a 12kHz shelf on it, and Apply soft-clipping limits the output
Menu — Panning law picks how the level is shared across the sweep: Linear, Equal power, or Linear clipped
Note — with the module bypassed each input is passed straight to the output on its own side
Compact oscillator with through-zero linear FM, a wavefolder and a VCA on its output, running as either a VCO or an LFO
Tunes the pitch, reaching 4 octaves either way on Full, 6 semitones on Octave, half a semitone on Semitone and 5 octaves either way on LFO
Picks how far FREQ reaches and whether the oscillator runs at audio rate or as an LFO: Full, Octave, Semitone or LFO
Sets the base pitch in octave steps from C1 at 32.7Hz up to C7, and in LFO mode the same steps run from 0.125Hz to 8Hz
Folds the sine, triangle and sawtooth waves harder as it rises, and on the pulse wave sets the pulse width instead
Picks the waveform at the output: sine, triangle, sawtooth or pulse
Linear frequency modulation that passes through zero, running the oscillator backwards on negative volts; its DC is filtered out by default
Adds to the TIMBRE slider, 0-10V covering its whole range
Volt-per-octave pitch, added to the FREQ knob and the OCT slider
A rising edge here restarts the waveform at the start of its cycle
Sets the output level, 0-10V from silence to full; with nothing patched the level is full
The chosen waveform, 10V peak to peak before the VCA
Menu — Hardware compatibility switches off the DC filter on the TZ-FM input, lifts the 5% to 95% limit on pulse width, and puts back the DC offset that an off-centre pulse has on the hardware
Menu — Oversampling runs the oscillator at up to eight times the sample rate to cut aliasing, with x2 the default
Three attenuator and inverter channels with a lamp ring on each showing the signal, cascading into one mix
Picks what that channel does and how its ring is lit: CV Inversion inverts the signal, CV Attenuation passes it as it stands, and Audio shows the level in dB
Attenuates that channel from silence to unity gain
The signal for that channel; with nothing patched it stands at a steady 10V, which makes the knob a constant source
That channel's signal attenuated and, in CV Inversion mode, inverted; patching it takes the channel out of the mix
The third channel's signal attenuated, with channels 1 and 2 added in when their own outputs have no cable
Menu — Hardware compatibility can stop the 10V normal being applied when a channel is set to Audio mode
Trigger processor: one trigger in produces a run of up to 32 triggers, spread across a window set by a tapped tempo
Switches between one burst per trigger and a burst that restarts itself as soon as the last one ends
Sets how many triggers a burst contains, 1 to 32
Starts a burst by hand, one per press
Attenuates the quantity CV, from nothing through to its full effect
Skews the spacing within the burst: even at noon, crowded at the start and slowing down clockwise, spread at the start and speeding up counter-clockwise
Multiplies or divides the tapped tempo to set the length of the burst window, by 2, 3, 4 or 5 either way, with the tempo itself at noon
Sets the chance that a trigger fires the whole burst rather than a single trigger, 100% counter-clockwise falling to 0% clockwise
Adds to the number of triggers in a burst, 5V adding sixteen, after the quantity attenuator
Skews the spacing within the burst, 10V covering the whole range, and is added to the distribution knob
Each pulse here sets the base tempo from the gap since the last one; a gap more than twice or less than half the one before it is discarded
Shifts the multiplication or division of the tempo, 10V covering four steps, and is added to the TIME DIV/MULT knob
Lowers the chance that a trigger fires the whole burst, 10V covering the whole range, and is added to the probability knob
A rising edge starts a burst
A 1ms 10V pulse at the base tempo, which runs at 2Hz until a ping sets it
A 1ms 10V pulse when a burst finishes; a burst cut short by the probability setting produces none
A 1ms 10V trigger for each event in the burst
Menu — Include original trigger in output puts the trigger that started the burst out as the burst's first trigger
Burst.notes: The sixteen-lamp ring around the quantity knob has no census index, so it has no line.

lines: Bridge to the MIDI Thing v2 hardware: twelve CV inputs sent out over MIDI to the unit's twelve assignable ports
Puts the connected MIDI Thing into the preset built for Rack and copies the current settings and voltage ranges over to it, one way only
A control voltage sent over MIDI to the matching port on the hardware; right-click its box on the panel to pick the range it expects, from 0-10V, -5V to 5V, 0-8V or 0-5V
Menu — Select MIDI Device picks the driver and output device the module sends to
Menu — All channels MIDI update rate sets the total rate shared between the active channels, from 250Hz to 8kHz, and the line under it shows what each active channel then gets
Menu — Set mode for all channels puts every port on the same voltage range in one go
Note — the hardware expects control voltages here, not audio-rate signals
Precision voltage source and adder, setting a voltage by octave and semitone for tuning and transposition
Adds a whole number of volts, 0 to 10, each step one octave at a volt per octave
Picks the span of the voltage set by hand: 0-10V, or -5V to 5V, which takes 5V off the octave setting
Adds a twelfth of a volt per step, one semitone at a time from C up to B
A voltage added to the one set by the two knobs
The voltage set by the octave and semitone knobs, with anything patched into the sum input added to it
Oscillator building six pulse waves an octave apart from one core, each with its own level slider, level CV and output
Attenuates the PWM input, from nothing through to its full effect
Tunes the pitch, reaching 4 octaves either way on Full, 1 octave on Octave and 1 semitone on Semitone
Sets the fundamental in octave steps, from C1 at 32.7Hz up to C7
Sets the pulse width of every octave, from 50% down to 0%
Picks how far the TUNE knob reaches: Full for 4 octaves either way, Octave for 1 octave, or Semitone for 1 semitone
Sets the level of that octave in the sum, from silence to full
Volt-per-octave pitch, added to the other V/OCT input and to the tuning controls
A rising edge here resets the core half way through its cycle, which hard-syncs all six octaves together
Modulates the pulse width of every octave, -10V to 10V covering the whole range, after the PWM attenuator
Scales the level of that octave, 0-10V spanning silence to the full level its slider sets; with nothing patched the level is whatever the slider says
Carries that octave's wave added to every lower octave whose own output has no cable, at 10V peak to peak
Menu — Hardware compatibility lifts the 5% to 95% limit on pulse width, puts back the DC offset that a narrow pulse has on the hardware, and swaps the pulse core for a triangle core
Menu — Oversampling runs the oscillator at up to eight times the sample rate to cut aliasing, with x4 the default
Stereo effects loop switched in and out by a gate, with a gain control and a choice of tails on the return
Picks what happens to the effects return when the loop is switched out: Hard cuts it dead, Soft leaves it running so reverb tails and delay repeats fade away
Sets the gain on the effects return, -30dB counter-clockwise through 0dB at noon to 12dB clockwise
Picks how the launch works: Latch toggles the loop on and off, Gate switches it in only while the trigger is high or the button is held
Switches the loop in and out by hand, toggling it in Latch mode and holding it in only while pressed in Gate mode
The left side of the signal going into the loop
The right side of the signal going into the loop; with nothing patched here the left input feeds both sides
The left side of the signal coming back from the effect
The right side of the signal coming back from the effect
Switches the loop in and out, toggling it on each rising edge in Latch mode and holding it in while high in Gate mode
The left side of the signal on its way to the effect, silent while the loop is switched out
The right side of the signal on its way to the effect, silent while the loop is switched out
The left side of the finished signal: the dry input when the loop is out, the effects return when it is in
The right side of the finished signal: the dry input when the loop is out, the effects return when it is in
Menu — Soft clip at ±10V saturates both outputs rather than letting them run past 10V
Menu — Slew time sets how long the switch takes to fade between dry and effect, from 5ms to 50ms, and is 10ms by default
Note — with the module bypassed each input is passed straight to the output on its own side
Bypass.notes: The slew time parameter (index 4) is a menu slider with no place on the panel, so it is untagged and covered by a Menu line instead.

lines: Four-band splitter and mixer: one signal cut into four bands, each with its own level, send and return, then summed back together
Sets the level of the low band below 300Hz before it is sent out
Sets the level of the low mid band around 750Hz before it is sent out
Sets the level of the high mid band around 1500Hz before it is sent out
Sets the level of the high band above 3000Hz before it is sent out
A signal into that band alone, added to whatever is at ALL IN
The signal for that band coming back from an effect; with nothing patched here the band's own send is used instead, unless that send has a cable of its own
Scales the level of that band, 0-10V from silence to the level its slider sets; with nothing patched the level is whatever the slider says
A signal fed into all four bands at once
Scales the whole mix, 0-10V from silence to full; with nothing patched the mix runs at full level
That band alone after its filter and level, taken out of the mix unless its return is patched
The four band returns added together and scaled by the mix level, soft-clipped at -10V to 10V
Menu — Soft clip at ±10V saturates the mix output rather than letting it run past 10V
Note — with the module bypassed every input is summed straight to the mix output with no filtering
Four-channel mixer for audio or CV in 4HP, split into two pairs that cascade into one master
Sets the level of that channel in the mix, from silence to unity gain
A signal into the mix, scaled by that channel's gain knob
Channels 1 and 2 added together; with no cable here that pair is passed on to the 3+4 output instead
Channels 3 and 4 added together, with channels 1 and 2 added in as well when the 1+2 output has no cable
Menu — Hardware compatibility can stop the outputs being clipped at -10V to 10V, which they are by default
Four attenuator and inverter channels whose inputs cascade into one another, so one signal can be split four ways
Attenuates that channel from silence to unity gain
Picks whether that channel passes its input as it stands or inverts it
The signal for that channel; with nothing patched, a channel takes the signal of the channel above it, and the topmost one takes a steady 10V
That channel's input, attenuated and inverted according to its own knob and switch
Menu — Normalled voltage sets what the topmost input falls back to when nothing is patched: +1V, +5V or +10V
Two voltage-controlled voltage processors, each working out A times B plus C, with switchable gain on both B and C
Attenuates the B input of that section, from silence at the bottom to its full level at the top
Sets the gain applied to the B input of that section before its attenuator: x-1, x1 or x2
Attenuates the C input of that section, from silence at the bottom to its full level at the top
Sets the gain applied to the C input of that section before its attenuator: x-1, x1 or x2
Picks what happens between the two sections: Mix adds section 1 into OUT2 whenever OUT 1 has no cable, and Mult normals a copy of A1 into the A2 input whenever A2 has no cable
One factor of the multiplication in that section; it is multiplied by B and divided by 5V
The other factor of the multiplication in that section, scaled by that section's B knob and gain switch; with nothing patched it stands at 5V, which turns the knob into a plain attenuator for A
The offset added to the product in that section, scaled by that section's C knob and gain switch; with nothing patched it stands at 5V, which turns the knob into an offset control
The first section's result, clipped at -10V to 10V
The second section's result, clipped at -10V to 10V, with the first section's result added in when the mode switch is on Mix and OUT 1 has no cable
Menu — Hardware compatibility can stop the outputs being clipped at -10V to 10V
Voltage-controlled lag processor with a slope detector, limiting how fast its output can follow its input
Bends the slope, straight counter-clockwise and increasingly curved clockwise as the gap to the input shrinks
Picks the span of the slew times: Fast is 4ms to 4 seconds, Medium 40ms to 40 seconds, Slow 400ms to 400 seconds, despite the source comment naming them the other way round
Sets how long the output takes to climb, longer the higher it goes; when the CV MODE switch routes the CV input to the rise, this slider attenuates that CV instead
Sets how long the output takes to drop, longer the higher it goes; when the CV MODE switch routes the CV input to the fall, this slider attenuates that CV instead
Chooses what the CV input controls: the fall time, both times, or the rise time
The signal to be slewed
Sets the slew time over 0-10V, attenuated by the slider for whichever stage the CV MODE switch has picked
The input signal with its rate of change limited by the rise and fall times
10V for as long as the output is climbing towards the input, and 0V otherwise
10V for as long as the output is dropping towards the input, and 0V otherwise
Slew.notes: The IN jack takes audio as readily as CV, so it has no family. The source comment naming the ranges is inverted against configSwitch: the switch reads Fast, Medium, Slow at values 0, 1, 2, and the times given here are computed from the code, not from the comment.

lines: Clock conditioner, multiple and divider in 2HP, giving the incoming clock and four halvings of it
The clock to be divided; every output changes on its rising edges
A rising edge here takes all four divided outputs low, leaving the undivided one alone
The incoming clock cleaned up to a 0-10V gate, high while the clock input is high
A 0-10V gate that flips state on every rising edge of the clock, so it runs at half the clock rate
A 0-10V gate that flips state on every rising edge of the half-rate output, so it runs at a quarter of the clock rate
A 0-10V gate that flips state on every rising edge of the quarter-rate output, so it runs at an eighth of the clock rate
A 0-10V gate that flips state on every rising edge of the eighth-rate output, so it runs at a sixteenth of the clock rate
Menu — Remove DC from clock outs shifts every output to -5V to 5V instead of 0-10V
Stereo effects processor in four sections: a filter, a resonator, a ping-pong echo and an ambience reverb, with a modulation source and per-knob CV and randomisation mapping
Sets the cutoff of the filter, from 10Hz to 22000Hz
Picks the filter type: lowpass, bandpass, highpass or comb
Moves the filter to one of four points in the chain, before or after the resonator, the echo and the ambience
Tunes the resonator
Spreads the resonator's partials away from a harmonic series
Sets how far the modulation source moves the parameters that have been mapped to it
Sets the rate of the modulation source
Picks the modulation shape: random, sine, ramp, inverted ramp, square, sample and hold, or envelope follower
Sets the resonance of the filter
Sets how much of the resonator's output is fed back into it
Sets the delay time of a two-tap stereo ping-pong echo, 10ms fully anti-clockwise out to 6 seconds fully clockwise; with a clock patched into SYNC the time is quantised to divisions of it
A single sweep that cuts the lows one way and the highs the other on the echo, leaving the signal untouched in the middle
Sets how many times the echo repeats
Sets the size, tone and direction of the ambience: smallest and brightest in the middle, biggest and darkest at either end, and running the input backwards below the middle
Pans the ambience from side to side on its own
Sets how long the ambience takes to die away
Sets the level of the filtered signal; when a cable is in the F.VCA jack this attenuates that CV instead
Sets how much resonator is mixed with the dry signal; when a cable is in the RESON jack this attenuates that CV instead
Sets how much echo is mixed with the dry signal; when a cable is in the ECHO jack this attenuates that CV instead
Sets how much ambience is mixed with the dry signal; when a cable is in the AMBIENCE jack this attenuates that CV instead
Picks what MAP applies to the knobs: randomisation, CV mapping, or modulation
Held down, it turns the knobs and buttons over to their second function
Fires a randomisation of everything the random mapping covers, which a trigger at the RANDOM input also does
Applies the mapping for whichever target the map mode names, so that turning a knob then sets that amount rather than the value
Wipes the mapping amounts for whichever target the map mode names
Sets how far the modulation source moves this parameter, from nothing to its full range
Sets how far the CV input moves this parameter, from nothing to its full range
Sets how far a randomisation event moves this parameter, from nothing to its full range
The left side of the signal going in, and with nothing patched on the right it feeds both sides in mono
The right side of the signal going in
Sets the dry and wet balance of that section, 0V to 5V, attenuated by that section's own mix knob
A clock for the time-based sections; with it patched the echo time snaps to divisions of the clock
A rising edge here fires a randomisation of everything the random mapping covers
Shifts the filter cutoff, -5V to 10V, scaled by the cutoff CV amount set through MAP
Shifts the resonator tuning, -5V to 10V, scaled by the tune CV amount set through MAP
Shifts the echo time, -5V to 10V, scaled by the echo CV amount set through MAP
Shifts the ambience spacetime, -5V to 10V, scaled by the spacetime CV amount set through MAP
The left side of the finished signal
The right side of the finished signal
Menu — Knob mode fixes which layer the knobs edit without holding a button: Normal, Alt, Mod, CV or Rnd
Menu — Use native VCV randomisation hands randomising over to Rack's own, and a slider there sets how long a randomisation takes to slew into place, from 0 to 10 seconds
Iroi.notes: The DSP for this module is not in the public repository, so the filter position ordering and the exact ranges of the resonator and ambience controls come from the maker's tooltips and the panel, not from code. The randomise slew time (param 48) is a menu slider with no place on the panel, so it is untagged and covered by a Menu line. A SYNC label appears on the panel near the MOD LEVEL knob with no control of its own at that spot; what it marks could not be settled.

lines: Eight channels of random voltage, one per trigger input, each with its own division, probability, quantising and looping
Sets the output level of that channel before any quantising
Counts incoming triggers on that channel and lets the output change only every 1 to 8 of them
Sets the chance from 0% to 100% that a trigger on that channel produces a new value
Picks the algorithm generating that channel's random values: Standard, Rosc, Gamma, Expo, Weibull, Low-High, FBM or Perlin
Adds a fixed 0-10V to that channel's output
Quantises that channel's output to a musical scale, with the leftmost position leaving it unquantised
Slews that channel's output from one value to the next, applied after quantising
Sets how many steps long that channel's loop is, from 1 to 32
A short press cycles that channel's looping between off, a locked loop, and a loop that mutates a step now and then; a long press opens that row's menu page, and a very long press resets the channel
A rising edge draws a new value on that channel, subject to its divider and its probability
That channel's random voltage, after gain, offset, quantising and slew
Menu — Load preset and Save preset move the whole state in and out of eight slots, the same slots the preset page reaches
Random8.notes: Each channel has one physical knob carrying eight stacked parameters, one per menu page, so those eight indices all sit at the same panel position and each has its own line. The channel buttons double as the menu page buttons, which is why one line covers both roles.
